Adam Smith, the "father of modern economics"
photo.description: Profile of Adam Smith. The original depiction of Smith was created in 1787 by James Tassie in the form of an enamel paste medallion. Smith did not usually sit for his portrait, so a considerable number of engravings and busts of Smith were made not from observation but from the same enamel medallion produced by Tassie, an artist who could convince Smith to sit.
photo.date: Original work in 1787. Etching produced in 1811, 1828 or 1872

photo.description: Cotton Mill Piecer, ca.1825 Image of a drawing of a piecer at work in a cotton mill. A piecer, normally a young child, had to lean over spinning machines to repair broken threads. The Scottish missionary David Livingstone (1813-1873) worked as a piecer from the age of 10 in Blantyre Cotton Mill.; This belongs to a series of Church of Scotland Foreign Missions Committee lantern slides relating to David Livingstone (1813-1873), the Scottish missionary who was best known as an explorer of Africa and anti-slavery campaigner.
